title: बुढीगण्डकीको बाढीले तहसनहस स्याउली बजार, करिब एक महिनासम्म पनि पीडितको पुनःस्थापना हुन सकेन
content:
गोरखा । असोज २५ गते बुढीगण्डकी नदीमा आएको भीषण बाढीले धादिङको त्रिपुरासुन्दरी -२ विशालनगर स्याउली बजारमा ठूलो क्षति पुर्‍याएको छ। बाढीले घर, खेतबारी, पशुचौपाया तथा घरभित्रका सामग्री बगाउनुका साथै कतिपय घर बस्नै नमिल्ने गरी क्षतिग्रस्त बनाएको छ। बाढी गएको करिब एक महिना बित्न लाग्दा पनि प्रभावित क्षेत्रको सरसफाइ, भग्नावशेष व्यवस्थापन र पीडितको पुनःस्थापनामा पर्याप्त ध्यान पुग्न नसकेको स्थानीयको गुनासो छ। बाढीले विशालनगर स्याउली बजारका स्थानीयको वर्षभरिको मेहनत र आम्दानीको स्रोतसमेत नष्ट गरेको छ। स्थानीय सुर श्रेष्ठका अनुसार बाढीले धानखेती लगाइएको खेत डुबानमा पारेर पूर्ण रूपमा नष्ट गरेको छ। करिब ५० मुरीसम्म धान उत्पादन हुने खेत बाढीले बगाएपछि यस वर्षको खाद्यान्न जोहो गर्ने आधारसमेत गुमेको उनले बताए। उनका अनुसार बजारमा बाढी आएको हल्ला फैलिएपछि स्थानीयले घरघरमा पुगेर सुरक्षित स्थानमा जान आग्रह गरेका थिए। त्यसपछि उनी र उनकी श्रीमतीले लगाउने कपडा झोलामा हालेर घर छाडेका थिए। दशैँ खर्चका लागि छुट्याएर राखेको ५० हजार रुपैयाँ खल्तीमा राखेर ज्यान जोगाउन निस्किएको क्षण सम्झँदै उनले बाढीले पुर्‍याएको क्षति अकल्पनीय रहेको बताए। ‘२५ सालमा पनि यस्तो बाढी आएको थियो। त्यसबेला घर बगाएको भए पनि अहिले जस्तो खेतबारीमा माथिसम्मै पुगेर रोपेको धान सबै बगाएको थिएन,’ उनले भने, ‘यसपालि त खेतमा लगाएको सबै बाली सखाप भयो।’ बाढीको त्रासदीसँगै घरबारविहीन भएका स्थानीयको पीडा अझै उस्तै छ। स्थानीय राजकुमार दाहालका अनुसार बाढी गएको लामो समय बितिसक्दा पनि प्रभावित बस्तीमा राज्यका तर्फबाट आवश्यक सरसफाइ र पुनःस्थापनाको काम हुन सकेको छैन। ढलेका घर, थुप्रिएको माटो र फोहोर हटाउने कामसमेत स्थानीयले आफ्नै खर्च र श्रममा गरिरहेका छन्। ‘बाढीले घर ढालेको छ, बाटो बन्द भएको छ। घरभित्र र वरपर थुप्रिएको माटो र भग्नावशेष हटाउन पनि आफैँ लाग्नुपरेको छ,’ उनले भने, ‘राज्यका तर्फबाट अहिलेसम्म प्रभावकारी सहयोग आएको छैन। विभिन्न संस्थाबाट आएको राहतसमेत फिर्ता गरिएको छ।’ दशैँका बेला घर गुमाएका बाढीपीडित चुलीदेवी विद्यालयको भवनमा आश्रय लिन पुगेका थिए। तर त्यहाँ बसोबास र खानपानको पर्याप्त व्यवस्था नहुँदा थप समस्या भोग्नुपरेको दाहालले बताए। उनका अनुसार बाढी प्रभावितको वास्तविक अवस्था बुझ्न र क्षतिग्रस्त बस्तीको अवलोकन गर्न जनप्रतिनिधि तथा सरोकारवाला निकाय नपुगेको स्थानीयको गुनासो छ। बाढीले क्षति पुर्‍याएको नयाँ पुल क्षेत्रमा मात्रै जनप्रतिनिधि तथा अन्य सरोकारवालाको ध्यान केन्द्रित भएको तर बस्तीभित्रको विनाशप्रति बेवास्ता गरिएको उनको आरोप छ। क्षतिग्रस्त सडक र बाटोसमेत स्थानीयले घरघरबाट बाटो खोल्दै आवतजावत सहज बनाउने प्रयास गरिरहेका छन्। डोजर आएर पनि बस्तीभित्रसम्म पुग्न सकेन। घर भत्काएर र स्थानीयको सहयोगमा बाटो खोल्नुपरेको छ,’ उनले भने, ‘हामीले ठूलो क्षति बेहोरेका छौँ, तर हाम्रो पीडा सुनिदिने र बोलिदिने कोही छैन। राज्यले हाम्रो अवस्था बुझोस्।’ बाढीको अर्को पीडादायी कथा राममाया घलेको छ। बाढीले उनको घरभित्रैसम्म माटो र गेग्रान थुपारेपछि घर बस्नै नमिल्ने भएको छ। घरभित्र रहेका खाद्यान्न, लत्ताकपडा तथा अन्य सामग्री डुबेर नष्ट भएका छन्। पशुचौपायासमेत बाढीको चपेटामा परेका छन्। बाख्रा फुकाएर ज्यान जोगाए पनि घरभित्रका सामान निकाल्न नपाएको उनले बताइन्। ‘घरभित्रसम्म माटो भरिएको छ। बस्न सक्ने अवस्था छैन। अब कहाँ जाने, कहाँ बस्ने भन्ने चिन्ता छ,’ उनले भनिन्, ‘माटो फाल्ने शक्ति छैन, साना छोराछोरी छन्। सहयोग गर्ने मान्छे पनि छैनन्।’ बाढीले घर र सम्पत्ति मात्र नभई पीडितको मानसिक अवस्थासमेत प्रभावित बनाएको छ। दशैँको समयमा आएको बाढीका कारण चाडपर्वको कुनै अनुभूति गर्न नपाएको घलेको भनाइ छ। घरभित्र पालेका बङ्गुर तथा अन्य पशुचौपायामा समेत क्षति पुगेपछि परिवारको जीविकोपार्जन थप संकटमा परेको छ। विशालनगर स्याउली बजारमा बाढीले घर, खेतबारी, सडक र स्थानीय पूर्वाधारमा क्षति पुर्‍याउँदा प्रभावित परिवार अहिले आधारभूत आवश्यकताकै अभावमा छन्। घरमा फर्केर बस्न सक्ने अवस्था छैन भने सुरक्षित आवास र पुनःस्थापनाको व्यवस्था पनि हुन सकेको छैन। स्थानीयले तत्काल राहत, सरसफाइ, आवास र जीविकोपार्जन पुनःस्थापनाका कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन गर्न सरकार तथा सम्बन्धित निकायसँग माग गरेका छन्। Gorkha. The severe flood in the Budhigandaki River on Asoj 25 has caused extensive damage to Syauli Bazaar, Bishalnagar, Tripurasundari-2, Dhading. The floods have swept away homes, farmlands, livestock, and household goods, and have damaged some homes to the point of making them uninhabitable. Even after nearly a month since the floods, locals complain that not enough attention has been paid to cleaning the affected areas, managing the debris, and rehabilitating the victims. The flood has destroyed the hard work and income of the locals of Bishalnagar Syauli Bazaar throughout the year. According to local Sur Shrestha, the flood has completely destroyed the rice fields. He said that after the flood swept away the fields that produced about 50 acres of rice, the basis for obtaining food for this year has also been lost. According to him, after the rumor of flooding in the market spread, locals went door to door and urged people to go to safer places. After that, he and his wife put the clothes they were wearing in a bag and left the house. Recalling the moment when he left for his life with the 50,000 rupees he had set aside for Dashain expenses in his pocket, he said that the damage caused by the flood was unimaginable. "Such a flood also occurred in 25 BS. Even though houses were washed away then, it did not reach the top of the fields and wash away all the rice that had been planted," he said. "This year, all the crops planted in the fields were destroyed." The pain of the locals who were left homeless by the flood tragedy is still the same. According to local Rajkumar Dahal, even after a long time since the flood, the state has not been able to carry out the necessary cleaning and rehabilitation work in the affected settlements. The locals are also doing the work of removing the collapsed houses, piled up soil, and garbage at their own expense and labor. "The flood has destroyed houses, blocked roads. We have to do our own work to remove the mud and debris piled up in and around our homes," he said. "So far, there has been no effective assistance from the state. Even the relief received from various organizations has been returned." Flood victims who lost their homes during Dashain had sought shelter in the Chuli Devi School building. However, Dahal said that they faced additional problems due to the lack of adequate accommodation and food facilities there. According to him, locals have complained that public representatives and concerned bodies have not reached the affected areas to understand the real situation of the flood victims and inspect the damaged settlements. He alleges that the attention of public representatives and other stakeholders has been focused only on the flood-damaged New Bridge area, but the destruction within the settlement has been ignored. Locals are trying to ease movement by opening up the damaged roads and paths from house to house. "Even when the bulldozer arrived, it could not reach the settlement. We had to demolish the houses and open the road with the help of the locals," he said. "We have suffered a lot of damage, but there is no one to listen to our pain and express it. The state should understand our situation." Another painful story of the flood is told by Rammaya Ghale. The flood has piled up mud and debris inside her house, making it uninhabitable. Food, clothes and other belongings inside the house have been submerged and destroyed. Even livestock have been affected by the flood. She said that even though she saved her life by releasing her goat, she was unable to remove the belongings inside the house. "The house is filled with mud. It is not possible to live in it. Now I am worried about where to go and where to live," she said. "I don't have the strength to shovel mud, I have small children. There is no one to help me." The flood has not only affected the houses and property but also the mental state of the victims. Ghale says that due to the floods that occurred during Dashain, they were not able to experience any of the festivities. The family's livelihood has been further jeopardized after the pigs and other livestock kept inside the house were also damaged. The flood in Syauli Bazaar, Bishalnagar, has damaged homes, farmlands, roads, and local infrastructure, leaving the affected families without basic necessities. They are unable to return home and have not been provided with safe housing and rehabilitation. Locals have demanded that the government and relevant agencies immediately implement relief, sanitation, housing, and livelihood restoration programs.

छन्। सहयोग गर्ने मान्छे पनि छैनन्।’ बाढीले घर र सम्पत्ति मात्र नभई पीडितको मानसिक अवस्थासमेत प्रभावित बनाएको छ। दशैँको समयमा आएको बाढीका कारण चाडपर्वको कुनै अनुभूति गर्न नपाएको घलेको भनाइ छ। घरभित्र पालेका बङ्गुर तथा अन्य पशुचौपायामा समेत क्षति पुगेपछि परिवारको जीविकोपार्जन थप संकटमा परेको छ। विशालनगर स्याउली बजारमा बाढीले घर, खेतबारी, सडक र स्थानीय पूर्वाधारमा क्षति पुर्‍याउँदा प्रभावित परिवार अहिले आधारभूत आवश्यकताकै अभावमा छन्। घरमा फर्केर बस्न सक्ने अवस्था छैन भने सुरक्षित आवास र पुनःस्थापनाको व्यवस्था पनि हुन सकेको छैन। स्थानीयले तत्काल राहत, सरसफाइ, आवास र जीविकोपार्जन पुनःस्थापनाका कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन गर्न सरकार तथा सम्बन्धित निकायसँग माग गरेका छन्।

गोरखा । असोज २५ गते बुढीगण्डकी नदीमा आएको भीषण बाढीले धादिङको त्रिपुरासुन्दरी -२ विशालनगर स्याउली बजारमा ठूलो क्षति पुर्‍याएको छ।

बाढीले घर, खेतबारी, पशुचौपाया तथा घरभित्रका सामग्री बगाउनुका साथै कतिपय घर बस्नै नमिल्ने गरी क्षतिग्रस्त बनाएको छ। बाढी गएको करिब एक महिना बित्न लाग्दा पनि प्रभावित क्षेत्रको सरसफाइ, भग्नावशेष व्यवस्थापन र पीडितको पुनःस्थापनामा पर्याप्त ध्यान पुग्न नसकेको स्थानीयको गुनासो छ।

बाढीले विशालनगर स्याउली बजारका स्थानीयको वर्षभरिको मेहनत र आम्दानीको स्रोतसमेत नष्ट गरेको छ। स्थानीय सुर श्रेष्ठका अनुसार बाढीले धानखेती लगाइएको खेत डुबानमा पारेर पूर्ण रूपमा नष्ट गरेको छ। करिब ५० मुरीसम्म धान उत्पादन हुने खेत बाढीले बगाएपछि यस वर्षको खाद्यान्न जोहो गर्ने आधारसमेत गुमेको उनले बताए।

उनका अनुसार बजारमा बाढी आएको हल्ला फैलिएपछि स्थानीयले घरघरमा पुगेर सुरक्षित स्थानमा जान आग्रह गरेका थिए। त्यसपछि उनी र उनकी श्रीमतीले लगाउने कपडा झोलामा हालेर घर छाडेका थिए। दशैँ खर्चका लागि छुट्याएर राखेको ५० हजार रुपैयाँ खल्तीमा राखेर ज्यान जोगाउन निस्किएको क्षण सम्झँदै उनले बाढीले पुर्‍याएको क्षति अकल्पनीय रहेको बताए।

‘२५ सालमा पनि यस्तो बाढी आएको थियो। त्यसबेला घर बगाएको भए पनि अहिले जस्तो खेतबारीमा माथिसम्मै पुगेर रोपेको धान सबै बगाएको थिएन,’ उनले भने, ‘यसपालि त खेतमा लगाएको सबै बाली सखाप भयो।’

बाढीको त्रासदीसँगै घरबारविहीन भएका स्थानीयको पीडा अझै उस्तै छ। स्थानीय राजकुमार दाहालका अनुसार बाढी गएको लामो समय बितिसक्दा पनि प्रभावित बस्तीमा राज्यका तर्फबाट आवश्यक सरसफाइ र पुनःस्थापनाको काम हुन सकेको छैन। ढलेका घर, थुप्रिएको माटो र फोहोर हटाउने कामसमेत स्थानीयले आफ्नै खर्च र श्रममा गरिरहेका छन्।

‘बाढीले घर ढालेको छ, बाटो बन्द भएको छ। घरभित्र र वरपर थुप्रिएको माटो र भग्नावशेष हटाउन पनि आफैँ लाग्नुपरेको छ,’ उनले भने, ‘राज्यका तर्फबाट अहिलेसम्म प्रभावकारी सहयोग आएको छैन। विभिन्न संस्थाबाट आएको राहतसमेत फिर्ता गरिएको छ।’

दशैँका बेला घर गुमाएका बाढीपीडित चुलीदेवी विद्यालयको भवनमा आश्रय लिन पुगेका थिए। तर त्यहाँ बसोबास र खानपानको पर्याप्त व्यवस्था नहुँदा थप समस्या भोग्नुपरेको दाहालले बताए। उनका अनुसार बाढी प्रभावितको वास्तविक अवस्था बुझ्न र क्षतिग्रस्त बस्तीको अवलोकन गर्न जनप्रतिनिधि तथा सरोकारवाला निकाय नपुगेको स्थानीयको गुनासो छ।

बाढीले क्षति पुर्‍याएको नयाँ पुल क्षेत्रमा मात्रै जनप्रतिनिधि तथा अन्य सरोकारवालाको ध्यान केन्द्रित भएको तर बस्तीभित्रको विनाशप्रति बेवास्ता गरिएको उनको आरोप छ। क्षतिग्रस्त सडक र बाटोसमेत स्थानीयले घरघरबाट बाटो खोल्दै आवतजावत सहज बनाउने प्रयास गरिरहेका छन्।

डोजर आएर पनि बस्तीभित्रसम्म पुग्न सकेन। घर भत्काएर र स्थानीयको सहयोगमा बाटो खोल्नुपरेको छ,’ उनले भने, ‘हामीले ठूलो क्षति बेहोरेका छौँ, तर हाम्रो पीडा सुनिदिने र बोलिदिने कोही छैन। राज्यले हाम्रो अवस्था बुझोस्।’

बाढीको अर्को पीडादायी कथा राममाया घलेको छ। बाढीले उनको घरभित्रैसम्म माटो र गेग्रान थुपारेपछि घर बस्नै नमिल्ने भएको छ। घरभित्र रहेका खाद्यान्न, लत्ताकपडा तथा अन्य सामग्री डुबेर नष्ट भएका छन्। पशुचौपायासमेत बाढीको चपेटामा परेका छन्। बाख्रा फुकाएर ज्यान जोगाए पनि घरभित्रका सामान निकाल्न नपाएको उनले बताइन्।

‘घरभित्रसम्म माटो भरिएको छ। बस्न सक्ने अवस्था छैन। अब कहाँ जाने, कहाँ बस्ने भन्ने चिन्ता छ,’ उनले भनिन्, ‘माटो फाल्ने शक्ति छैन, साना छोराछोरी छन्। सहयोग गर्ने मान्छे पनि छैनन्।’

बाढीले घर र सम्पत्ति मात्र नभई पीडितको मानसिक अवस्थासमेत प्रभावित बनाएको छ। दशैँको समयमा आएको बाढीका कारण चाडपर्वको कुनै अनुभूति गर्न नपाएको घलेको भनाइ छ। घरभित्र पालेका बङ्गुर तथा अन्य पशुचौपायामा समेत क्षति पुगेपछि परिवारको जीविकोपार्जन थप संकटमा परेको छ।

विशालनगर स्याउली बजारमा बाढीले घर, खेतबारी, सडक र स्थानीय पूर्वाधारमा क्षति पुर्‍याउँदा प्रभावित परिवार अहिले आधारभूत आवश्यकताकै अभावमा छन्। घरमा फर्केर बस्न सक्ने अवस्था छैन भने सुरक्षित आवास र पुनःस्थापनाको व्यवस्था पनि हुन सकेको छैन।

स्थानीयले तत्काल राहत, सरसफाइ, आवास र जीविकोपार्जन पुनःस्थापनाका कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन गर्न सरकार तथा सम्बन्धित निकायसँग माग गरेका छन्।

Gorkha. The severe flood in the Budhigandaki River on Asoj 25 has caused extensive damage to Syauli Bazaar, Bishalnagar, Tripurasundari-2, Dhading. The floods have swept away homes, farmlands, livestock, and household goods, and have damaged some homes to the point of making them uninhabitable. Even after nearly a month since the floods, locals complain that not enough attention has been paid to cleaning the affected areas, managing the debris, and rehabilitating the victims. The flood has destroyed the hard work and income of the locals of Bishalnagar Syauli Bazaar throughout the year. According to local Sur Shrestha, the flood has completely destroyed the rice fields. He said that after the flood swept away the fields that produced about 50 acres of rice, the basis for obtaining food for this year has also been lost. According to him, after the rumor of flooding in the market spread, locals went door to door and urged people to go to safer places. After that, he and his wife put the clothes they were wearing in a bag and left the house. Recalling the moment when he left for his life with the 50,000 rupees he had set aside for Dashain expenses in his pocket, he said that the damage caused by the flood was unimaginable. "Such a flood also occurred in 25 BS. Even though houses were washed away then, it did not reach the top of the fields and wash away all the rice that had been planted," he said. "This year, all the crops planted in the fields were destroyed." The pain of the locals who were left homeless by the flood tragedy is still the same. According to local Rajkumar Dahal, even after a long time since the flood, the state has not been able to carry out the necessary cleaning and rehabilitation work in the affected settlements. The locals are also doing the work of removing the collapsed houses, piled up soil, and garbage at their own expense and labor. "The flood has destroyed houses, blocked roads. We have to do our own work to remove the mud and debris piled up in and around our homes," he said. "So far, there has been no effective assistance from the state. Even the relief received from various organizations has been returned." Flood victims who lost their homes during Dashain had sought shelter in the Chuli Devi School building. However, Dahal said that they faced additional problems due to the lack of adequate accommodation and food facilities there. According to him, locals have complained that public representatives and concerned bodies have not reached the affected areas to understand the real situation of the flood victims and inspect the damaged settlements. He alleges that the attention of public representatives and other stakeholders has been focused only on the flood-damaged New Bridge area, but the destruction within the settlement has been ignored. Locals are trying to ease movement by opening up the damaged roads and paths from house to house. "Even when the bulldozer arrived, it could not reach the settlement. We had to demolish the houses and open the road with the help of the locals," he said. "We have suffered a lot of damage, but there is no one to listen to our pain and express it. The state should understand our situation." Another painful story of the flood is told by Rammaya Ghale. The flood has piled up mud and debris inside her house, making it uninhabitable. Food, clothes and other belongings inside the house have been submerged and destroyed. Even livestock have been affected by the flood. She said that even though she saved her life by releasing her goat, she was unable to remove the belongings inside the house. "The house is filled with mud. It is not possible to live in it. Now I am worried about where to go and where to live," she said. "I don't have the strength to shovel mud, I have small children. There is no one to help me." The flood has not only affected the houses and property but also the mental state of the victims. Ghale says that due to the floods that occurred during Dashain, they were not able to experience any of the festivities. The family's livelihood has been further jeopardized after the pigs and other livestock kept inside the house were also damaged. The flood in Syauli Bazaar, Bishalnagar, has damaged homes, farmlands, roads, and local infrastructure, leaving the affected families without basic necessities. They are unable to return home and have not been provided with safe housing and rehabilitation. Locals have demanded that the government and relevant agencies immediately implement relief, sanitation, housing, and livelihood restoration programs.
